newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS-EU opens probe into French aid to Thomson.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-EU opens probe into French aid to Thomson.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday it had opened a formal probe into the recapitalisation of Thomson Multimedia (TMM), a unit of French state-owned defence and consumer electronics giant Thomson SA.

It said the French government had requested clearance for its plan to inject 11 billion francs ($2.09 billion) into Thomson SA and its debt-laden multimedia division, whose controversial sale to Daewoo Electronics was recently cancelled.
The statement did not give details on the injection shareout, but Commission sources said that TMM would get the bulk of it.

The recapitalisation of Thomson SA was initially due to benefit marginally its defence electronics arm Thomson-CSF, but the plan was modified after the French government cancelled the group's privatisation.

Paris had agreed on the sale of Thomson SA to French group Lagardere which in turn would have divested TMM to Daewoo Electronics. But the operation fell apart under the opposition of a parliamentary privatisation commission to the second aspect of the operation.
TMM's brand names include Telefunken and Brandt for television sets. It is also world leader in digital television.
France's new intention is to sell Thomson-CSF separately early next year while proceeding with the restructuring of TMM, which at the end of 1995 had debts of 13.8 billion francs.
The Commission left no doubt on Wednesday that the state cash injection into TMM amounted to subsidies.

It also queried the purchase by the French state of Thomson's participation in state-controlled Credit Lyonnais, one of France's largest banks which is currently being rescued under the Commission's close scrutiny.
It said the shares could have been over-valued but did not elaborate on the price paid to Thomson, and by how much it thought it had been overvalued.
The Commission's probe apparently only concerns Thomson SA's three percent stake in Lyonnais, not Thomson-CSF's direct shareholding of about 17 percent, the Commission sources said.
But the final decision on whether the price was inflated was likely to affect both operations, the sources said.
The Commission can block state subsidies if it feels they affect fair competition in the 15-nation European Union.
In practice, it clears most state aid plans under the strict condition that the company's long-term viability be restored. This usually implies capacity cuts.
Rival Dutch company Philips Electronics has been watching the Commission's reaction carefully in the TMM case, Commission officials said.
There is no deadline for a final ruling. $1 = 5.24 French francs
